_meta.title: TriageWiseProdrome — explanation builder cases (reqs 1.8, 1.8-T)
_meta.validates: ExplanationBuilder.build(severity_result, intake) → Explanation — the 4-part XAI object
_meta.how_to_use: Each case: build a SeverityResult + intake, call build(), assert the Explanation's four fields exactly. named_drivers must trace 1:1 to fired rules (no invented drivers). gap_acknowledgement must contain all 4 gap keys.

explanation_shape.data_completeness: string, form 'N of 5' (scoreable vitals: SpO2, HR, RR, SBP, pain)
explanation_shape.named_drivers: list[Driver] — one per fired rule; factor, threshold, patient_value, weight, contribution_pct
explanation_shape.gap_acknowledgement: dict with keys: not_provided, assumed, recorded_not_scored, red_flag_input, beyond_the_data (each a list; empty list when none)

conventions: data_completeness denominator is 5 (scoreable fields), never 7 or 8.
named_drivers come straight from severity_result.named_drivers — the builder must not add, drop, or invent any.
not_provided / assumed come from the scoreable vitals (missing_fields + fallbacks_applied).
recorded_not_scored comes from the INTAKE — non-scoreable fields the patient DID provide (temperature, blood_sugar, blood_pressure_diastolic).

red_flag_input comes from the INTAKE — source-qualified strings naming the field and value that fed a fired flag, e.g. 'Pre-existing conditions: diabetes', 'Symptoms: fast_positive'. Preserves which bucket each input came from.
beyond_the_data is a fixed list, same every case.
fallback_instruction is a constant — identical in every case.

recorded_not_scored vs red_flag_input are mutually exclusive: a non-scoreable field that FED a fired flag (e.g. temperature driving flag 8/10, or the borderline count) goes to red_flag_input; if it fed no flag it stays in recorded_not_scored. red_flag_input wins.
beyond_the_data_fixed: Appearance, work of breathing, distress, social context, staffing - outside this engine.
